leads.title: French Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810
leads.documents: Decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity in private in France; basis for legal status in Saint Barthelemy as French territory applying French criminal law.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as Penal Code of 1791 made no mention of same-sex relations in private, retained in Penal Code of 1810 and followed in nations and French colonies that adopted the Code

leads.title: Vichy Article 334 / Article 331 - unequal age of consent law
leads.documents: Former discriminatory age of consent (21 then 18 for homosexual relations vs 15 for heterosexual); documents repeal and equalization relevant to sexual-offences enforcement history.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: introduced 6 Aug 1942 as article 334, moved to article 331 on 8 Feb 1945, lowered to 18 in 1974, repealed 4 Aug 1982 under President Francois Mitterrand to equalise at 15

leads.title: Article 330 alinea 2 Penal Code - Mirguet amendment (1960) and 2024 compensation bill
leads.documents: Former doubled penalty for indecent exposure for homosexual activity; repeal history and state compensation effort for pre-1980 arrests.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: adopted 1960 via ordonnance authorized to fight alcoholism, sub-amendment by Paul Mirguet; repealed 1980; March 2024 National Assembly unanimous bill for compensation regarding gay men arrested under Article 330 prior to 1980, Senate yet to vote

leads.title: Law of 17 May 2013 opening marriage to same-sex couples - Journal Officiel 19 May 2013 and Constitutional Council ruling 17 May 2013
leads.documents: Legalizes same-sex marriage and joint adoption throughout France including all overseas departments and territories including Saint Barthelemy; constitutional validation.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: National Assembly 329-229 on 12 Feb 2013, Senate approval 12 April, National Assembly acceptance 23 April, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 May 2013, signed by President Francois Hollande 18 May 2013, published Journal Officiel next day, first ceremony 29 May Montpellier

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on modernisation of justice - transgender legal gender change, effective 1 Jan 2017
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without surgery, sterilisation, psychiatrist certificates; requires court order; first-name change at registry office - core gender-recognition machinery for trans visitors/residents.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: Senate approved 6 Nov 2015, National Assembly 24 May 2016 and modified version 12 July 2016, Senate discussed 28 Sept, National Assembly plenary 12 Oct rejected medical-treatment amendments, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov 2016, published Journal Officiel next day, took effect 1 Jan 2017; introduced by MP Pascale Crozon

leads.title: Article 225-1 French Penal Code and Labour Code Chapter 2 - discrimination protections
leads.documents: Prohibits discrimination on sexual orientation (1985) and sexual identity/gender identity (2012/2016) in employment, housing, goods/services - primary anti-discrimination protection applicable in Saint Barthelemy.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: 1985 national legislation; July 2012 added sexual identity synonymous with gender identity; 18 Nov 2016 amended article 225-1 to replace sexual identity with gender identity; Labour Code quote listing origin, gender, morals, sexual orientation, gender identity etc.

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 amending anti-discrimination legislation and Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881
leads.documents: Criminalizes homophobic/sexist/racist comments, injury/defamation/insult/incitement; increases penalties for assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation; created Haute autorite de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'egalite - hate-crime enforcement machinery.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: National Assembly approved 31 Dec 2004, max penalty 45,000 euro fine and/or 12 months imprisonment; Title 3 and articles 20 and 21 amended Press Law of 29 July 1881; first conviction Jan 2006 of MP Christian Vanneste later cancelled by Court of Cassation; 2017 transphobia became aggravating cause for all crimes punishable by prison

leads.title: B. v France - European Court of Human Rights (1992)
leads.documents: Court ruling that required France to allow legal gender change after decades-long legislative ban, even with medical/surgical transition; foundational trans-rights precedent.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: cited as 1992 case B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changed ban; context includes 1959 Coccinelle legal change with lawyer Robert Badinter and 1962 marriage recognition before ban

leads.title: Law prohibiting conversion therapy - published 1 February 2022
leads.documents: Bans conversion therapy with 2 years imprisonment and/or 30,000 euro fine; documents state protection against pseudoscientific practices including electroconvulsive therapy, exorcisms, talk therapy.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: MP Laurence Vanceunebrock-Mialon proposal announced summer 2019, Senate passed 7 Dec 2020, National Assembly concurred 25 Jan 2022, officially published 1 Feb 2022; Le Refuge estimate 3-4% helpline calls

leads.title: ILGA-Europe 2022 report on gender-affirming healthcare in France and DILCRAH / overseas attitudes data
leads.documents: Institutional/human-rights monitoring: lack of self-determination, waiting times, inequitable access, recommendation for informed consent; DILCRAH Interministerial Delegation for Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism and Anti-LGBT Hatred as rights machinery; plus 2014 study and parliamentary vote data contextualizing Saint Barthelemy - same-sex marriage legal in all overseas, deputy for Saint Martin and Saint Barthelemy voted against, but Saint Barthelemy described as more open/relaxed due to international celebrity tourism vs other French Caribbean.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation detail: ILGA-Europe report published 2022; DILCRAH scientific committee controversy 2022 involving Little Mermaid Observatory; overseas deputies vote: 11 for, 11 against including 1 from Saint Martin and Saint Barthelemy, 1 abstained, 3 absent; 2014 study: about 20% of overseas residents saw homosexuality as sexuality like any other vs 77% metropolitan France
